metadata.title: Dow futures near 53,000 as chip stocks attempt rebound

content.text:
U.S. stock futures pointed higher Monday after a three-day break over the Fourth of July holiday weekend. Nasdaq futures climbed 1.1%, while S&P 500 futures added 0.4% and Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were hovering flat near the 53,000 milestone.
Tech stocks led early gains. Western Digital stock advanced roughly 3% and Teradyne jumped about 4%, helping lift the State Street Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF by more than 1%. Marvell Technology and Oracle each posted gains of more than 3% and more than 2%, respectively.
The rebound in tech came after a difficult stretch for semiconductors. Chipmakers extended their pullback, with the VanEck Semiconductor ETF dropping 3.2% to log a second straight week of losses. Mark Newton, head of technical strategy at Fundstrat, noted the weakness had not undermined the broader market. "The broadening in sector rotation is a big positive, with Financials, Healthcare, and Industrials all closing at new weekly all-time highs this week and more than offsetting the consolidation in Semis," Newton wrote, according to CNBC. "While the Semi decline is a short-term headwind that favors owning other sectors while it settles, it has not dented the broader indices."
Last week's rally pushed the Nasdaq Composite up 2.1%, while the S&P 500 rose 1.8%.
Investor attention this week will center on the Federal Reserve. Fed minutes covering Kevin Warsh's inaugural meeting as chair will be released Wednesday, a document investors will scrutinize for any hints about where borrowing costs are headed.
The week also carries several tests for AI-related appetite. A quarterly business update from Samsung arrives Tuesday, while SK Hynix's planned $29 billion U.S. listing — which would place it among the most valuable share offerings ever recorded — is expected to price later in the week. SpaceX is also set to join the Nasdaq-100 on Tuesday.
Elsewhere in markets, crude prices slipped after the OPEC+ alliance voted to expand production for the fifth consecutive month. Having touched a four-decade trough against the dollar in the prior week, the yen stood at 162.24 to the dollar on Monday. Across the Atlantic, the pan-European Stoxx 600 edged down 0.2% amid subdued trading, and a mixed session wrapped up across Asia-Pacific.
